summary: ARES Mission Control is an autonomous 3D Martian survival and navigation system designed for the "Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map" challenge. On Mars, a 4-to-24-minute Earth-Mars radio delay prevents live rescue during emergencies, while straight-line paths often cross >20° crater cliffs and -95°C cold traps that triple metabolic oxygen burn. ARES fuses real NASA Mars Trek orbital datasets (MOLA Elevation, Viking Color, THEMIS Thermal) and rover imagery with a client-side Edge MLP Terrain Classifier and Weighted A* solver to compute physics-verified, oxygen-safe routes. Featuring a 3D Mars Open-World Globe, manual W-A-S-D rover driving, offline Web Audio step-sync, and real-time PLSS oxygen depletion with AI voice return alerts, ARES empowers astronauts to survive and navigate Mars independently.
details:
What It Does & How It Works:

ARES Mission Control is a real-time, offline-capable 3D Martian navigation cockpit built for surface astronauts and rovers. It combines an Open-World 3D Mars Globe (featuring 5 discovered NASA rover zones and unexplored planetary sectors) with a high-resolution 3D Terrain Explorer. Using a client-side Edge MLP Terrain Classifier (<0.8ms inference) and an 8-directional Weighted A* pathfinder, ARES evaluates local slope, surface roughness, regolith drag, and THEMIS thermal anomalies to plot a Solar Amber Safe Corridor that bypasses >20° cliffs and -95°C cold traps.

Survival Physics & Interactive Controls:

- Tobler’s Hiking Function & PLSS Oxygen Model: Dynamically adjusts movement speed under Mars's 0.38g gravity and computes slope-weighted oxygen burn from a 420-liter spacesuit tank (29.6 kPa cabin pressure).

- Manual W-A-S-D Rover Drive & Hill Counter: Users drive the rover directly across craters and the planetary globe while tracking hills traversed and gradual O2 depletion.

- Offline Acoustic Step-Sync: Uses the browser Web Audio API to detect real footsteps offline and advance the astronaut 0.85m per stride.

- Two-Tier Critical O2 Alert & AI Voice Warning: At <=30% and <=15% oxygen, ARES triggers an AI-synthesized voice warning and plots an immediate Emergency Short-Cut Extraction Route back to base camp.

Tools, Languages & NASA Data Used:

Built with Three.js (WebGL), GSAP, HTML5 Canvas 2D, Web Audio API, Web Speech API, and vanilla ES6+ JavaScript/CSS3, powered by NASA Mars Trek WMTS (MOLA, Viking MDIM 2.1, THEMIS) and NASA Image & Video Library APIs.
